text:
tessa: Quick flag — onboarding README has env var drift. Top shows API_HOST but snippets use REDWOOD_API_KEY. Users get 401.

omar: Where is this?

tessa: examples/onboarding/README.md, network snippet. Current JS uses process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN and curl uses API_HOST+?token=.

ben: Oof. We should standardize to REDWOOD_API_URL (with https://) and REDWOOD_API_KEY, and always show Authorization: Bearer in curl.

omar: Agreed. Small checklist: 1) replace API_HOST/API_TOKEN/REDWOOD_TOKEN -> REDWOOD_API_URL/REDWOOD_API_KEY, 2) remove query param auth, 3) add note that SDKs set the header when constructed with apiKey.

tessa: Proposed curl block to paste: `export REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-REPLACE_ME && curl "$REDWOOD_API_URL/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}'`

ben: Also fix the Node snippet to use fetch and process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, and add a short footnote for Windows env variants.

docs-bot: created docs issue #4219 to track env/auth parity.

ci-bot: FYI PR linked failed docs-lint due to missing blank line before fenced code block.

omar: I'll open a tiny docs PR with the changes and run `make docs-lint` before assigning. Thanks for catching this.
